panels.description:
P50, P90, P95, P99, and P99.9 TTFT latency in seconds.

Quantiles are computed per rate window: requests slower than the rest only move the Pn line if they make up more than (1 - n) of that window's traffic. A handful of 60s requests among a few hundred fast ones stays invisible on P99 even though users clearly feel it. Use the heatmap on the right to locate the tail, and widen the time range with care - a longer $__rate_interval dilutes rare spikes further.

Measured by the inference engine, so it excludes gateway, proxy and network time; client-observed TTFT is always greater than or equal to this.

panels.description:
Estimated TFLOP/s per GPU. Divide by the accelerator's peak dense FLOP/s for the MFU percentage — the dashboard cannot do that for you, because the peak is a property of the hardware rather than of the series.

This is the prefill-side question: processing a prompt is compute bound, so how close it runs to peak is how well the engine is batching. Generation is memory bound and will sit far below peak here no matter how healthy it is — judge that on the bandwidth panel beside this one.

On a disaggregated deployment read this per role instead, on the PD dashboard: measured on a live 1P1D, prefill ran at 6.9 FLOP per byte against decode's 0.82, so one figure over both describes neither.

**Supported backends:** vLLM and SGLang, both only with `--enable-mfu-metrics` in the model's backend parameters. It is off by default on both, and the two behave differently when it is off: SGLang does not register the counters, so this panel is empty; vLLM registers them anyway and leaves them at exactly 0, so a flat zero line means the flag is missing, not that the GPUs are idle. Measured 2026-09-21 on four live vLLM engines: all three families present, all at 0.0.

Averaged across instances, never summed: the counter is already per GPU, so a sum divided by one device's peak is meaningless. vLLM's own multi-engine logger declines to aggregate these for the same reason.

Source: `gpustack:estimated_flops_per_gpu`
panels.title: Compute Throughput per GPU (MFU)

panels.description:
Estimated bytes per second moved to and from HBM per GPU — read plus write. Divide by the accelerator's HBM bandwidth for the MBU percentage.

This is the one that usually caps token generation. Every output token re-reads the KV cache, so a serving engine saturates bandwidth long before it saturates FLOPs; when this approaches the device's bandwidth, more replicas is the remaining lever.

**Supported backends:** vLLM and SGLang, both only with `--enable-mfu-metrics` in the model's backend parameters. It is off by default on both, and the two behave differently when it is off: SGLang does not register the counters, so this panel is empty; vLLM registers them anyway and leaves them at exactly 0, so a flat zero line means the flag is missing, not that the GPUs are idle. Measured 2026-09-21 on four live vLLM engines: all three families present, all at 0.0.

Averaged across instances, never summed: the counter is already per GPU, so a sum divided by one device's peak is meaningless. vLLM's own multi-engine logger declines to aggregate these for the same reason.

Source: `gpustack:estimated_{read,write}_bytes_per_gpu`
